requirements.requirement: Prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading immediately on node1.
requirements.summary: The module was absent, modprobe resolved usb-storage to /bin/false, an actual load request was rejected, and the module remained absent.

requirements.requirement: Keep usb-storage blocked after a reboot.
requirements.summary: Persistent modprobe and initramfs configuration was installed, the initramfs omitted the driver, and after a confirmed reboot the module remained absent and an actual load request was rejected.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution, node1 ran CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64. The implementation used functioning platform-native modprobe and dracut facilities, with no package replacement or OS/kernel change observed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Restart evidence shows a healthy pre-restart system, an acknowledged native reboot, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, recovered system and root-filesystem state, no failed units, and persistent rejection of usb-storage loading.
limitations: No physical USB mass-storage hot-plug test was captured; enforcement was instead demonstrated through actual modprobe rejection, module-state checks, initramfs inspection, and post-reboot verification.

The restart protocol did not probe a separate application data workload or multi-node cluster state; none was identified in this single-node, host-configuration task. Recovery evidence covers system state, failed units, root filesystem, and the configured module policy.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had a clear task role: writing the persistent block configuration, rebuilding the current initramfs, testing module loading, and rebooting for persistence verification. No unrelated or troubleshooting-only mutation is shown. The sole hygiene defect is that two bounded test-output files created by cmd-58c4a85fa87544ec and cmd-d6a9250cd43e4018 remained in /tmp rather than being cleaned up; this was retained low-risk residue. No failed services, new exposure, or package damage was observed.
